understanding.goal_understanding: Progress through all KA59 levels by moving/click-selecting the available selectable pieces so that every goal tile marked with a '+' is simultaneously occupied by a selectable piece; a level is only won when all its goal tiles are covered at the same time, and the entire game is won after triggering WIN on the final level within the step budget.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each turn controls the currently selected piece (shown as 'P' in the semantic grid) using MOVE_* actions that shift it by one grid cell (3 pixels) in the chosen direction; other selectable pieces are shown as 'S' and can be controlled by using CLICK with their exact pixel/grid position. Movement can be blocked by walls/boundaries (#) and objects, though the movement.*_blocked flags are only hints and do not perfectly predict success. Some objects (blocks 'B') are pushable: if a pushable is immediately adjacent in the move direction, the move can push it along with the selected piece provided space allows; otherwise the move is prevented. Walls generally stop movement/pushing, but some boundary behaviors can be nonstandard and need to be tested in play.

understanding.goal_understanding: Progress through all KA59 levels by moving/click-selecting the available selectable pieces so that every goal tile marked with a '+' is simultaneously occupied by a selectable piece; a level is only won when all its goal tiles are covered at the same time, and the entire game is won after triggering WIN on the final level within the step budget.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Each turn controls the currently selected piece (shown as 'P' in the semantic grid) using MOVE_* actions that shift it by one grid cell (3 pixels) in the chosen direction; other selectable pieces are shown as 'S' and can be controlled by using CLICK with their exact pixel/grid position. Movement can be blocked by walls/boundaries (#) and objects, though the movement.*_blocked flags are only hints and do not perfectly predict success. Some objects (blocks 'B') are pushable: if a pushable is immediately adjacent in the move direction, the move can push it along with the selected piece provided space allows; otherwise the move is prevented. Walls generally stop movement/pushing, but some boundary behaviors can be nonstandard and need to be tested in play.
